_note: Slots for [brg_community-give]. The `slides` repeater was wired by conti 2026-09-23 at Sean's request — finn owns this file, same arrangement as team-members. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {{token}} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. `text`/`textarea` defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`.\n\nTHE LEDE IS THREE SLOTS, NOT ONE, because it wraps an inline <b> and no field may carry HTML. The spaces either side of the <b> live in the markup on purpose: ACF trims on save, so a default ending in a space would lose it and the words would run together.

lede_1.label: Lede — before the emphasis
lede_1.doc: Opening clause, ending at the em dash. The space before the emphasized phrase is in the markup, so do not add a trailing space here. Write the em dash as a literal —.
lede_1.default: At BRG, community isn't a marketing initiative —

lede_emphasis.label: Lede — emphasized phrase
lede_emphasis.doc: Rendered in the display face, slightly larger, mid-sentence. Short — a clause, not a sentence.

lede_2.label: Lede — after the emphasis
lede_2.doc: The rest of the paragraph. The space after the emphasized phrase is in the markup, so start straight in with a capital.
lede_2.default: When our restaurants thrive, the people around us should feel that too. That means showing up at local events, supporting causes that matter, partnering with schools and nonprofits, and investing in the places our guests call home.

banner.label: Teal banner
banner.doc: The rotated teal band straddling the white intro and the dark slider. Sized to its content (width:max-content, capped at 92%) so length is forgiving, but it renders at up to 3rem — past ~28 characters it starts wrapping and the rotation reads badly.

slides.label: Slides
slides.doc:
One row per slide, in the order they appear. Drag to reorder. Any number works: the slider builds its own dots, and the panel color alternates black / yellow by position, so adding or removing a slide re-colors the rest automatically — do not try to set a color per slide. Until the first row is added the page keeps the three slides it shows today.

Each slide's two buttons carry their own size, color, hover color, fill and hover effect. Left on "Same as the section" they follow the Buttons settings for this section below, which in turn follow the Site-wide page.

photo.label: Photo
photo.doc: Fills the image half of the slide, cropped to fit, so the exact size does not matter. Portrait or landscape both work. A tall crop around 1200px on the long edge is plenty — bigger files only slow the page.

photo_tone.label: Photo — color
photo_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

photo_px.label: Photo — movement
photo_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

photo_px_dir.label: Photo — movement direction
photo_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

photo_float.label: Photo — frame drift
photo_float.doc: Moves the whole frame across the section, on top of the movement inside it, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off; 8 and 12 were the old Gentle and Strong. 40 is the ceiling. Leave this off for a photo that fills its section edge to edge — there is nothing behind it to reveal.

photo_float_dir.label: Photo — drift direction
photo_float_dir.doc: Which way this frame drifts. Set a large and a small photo in opposite directions.

title.label: Title
title.doc: Shown in the display face, uppercase. Short — around 24 characters keeps it on one line.

body.label: Text
body.doc: The paragraph under the title, capped at 44 characters wide. Around 200 characters sits best; much longer and the panel grows taller than the photo beside it.

cta_label.label: Button label
cta_label.doc: Optional. Leave blank and no button appears. Two or three words, e.g. 'Apply for a donation'.

cta_href.label: Button link
cta_href.doc: Where the button goes — a full https:// address, or a path on this site like /contact/. Ignored when the label is blank.

cta_popup.label: Open in a pop-up
cta_popup.doc: Choose Pop-up for a Google Form and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people away to Google. The panel matches the site; the FORM's own colors are set on the form itself, under Theme in Google Forms — nothing on this site can reach inside it. Anything that is not a form should stay on Open the link.

cta_size.label: Button — size
cta_size.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow the section's Size under Buttons below.

cta_color.label: Button — color
cta_color.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Button color under Buttons below. Set it to make one button stand out from the others — a main button and a quieter second one, for instance.

cta_hover.label: Button — hover color
cta_hover.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Button hover color under Buttons below. Set it to give one button its own hover — a main button that flips to black while the quieter ones stay put.

cta_style.label: Button — filled or outline
cta_style.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow the section's setting under Buttons below. The usual pair is a filled main button next to an outline one.

cta_effect.label: Button — hover effect
cta_effect.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Hover effect, which in turn follows the site-wide one on the Site-wide page. Set it here to make one button behave differently from its neighbors.

cta2_label.label: Second button label
cta2_label.doc: Leave empty for a slide that needs only one button. This one sits beside the first.

cta2_popup.label: Second button — open in a pop-up
cta2_popup.doc: Choose Pop-up for a Google Form and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people away to Google. The panel matches the site; the FORM's own colors are set on the form itself, under Theme in Google Forms — nothing on this site can reach inside it. Anything that is not a form should stay on Open the link.

cta2_size.label: Second button — size
cta2_size.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow the section's Size under Buttons below.

cta2_color.label: Second button — color
cta2_color.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Button color under Buttons below. Set it to make one button stand out from the others — a main button and a quieter second one, for instance.

cta2_hover.label: Second button — hover color
cta2_hover.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Button hover color under Buttons below. Set it to give one button its own hover — a main button that flips to black while the quieter ones stay put.

cta2_style.label: Second button — filled or outline
cta2_style.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow the section's setting under Buttons below. The usual pair is a filled main button next to an outline one.

cta2_effect.label: Second button — hover effect
cta2_effect.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Hover effect, which in turn follows the site-wide one on the Site-wide page. Set it here to make one button behave differently from its neighbors.

video_id.label: Background video (optional)
video_id.doc: Paste a YouTube or Vimeo link, or just the ID. Leave blank and the photo above is used. The video plays silently on a loop with no controls, and the photo shows while it loads, if the video is blocked, or for visitors who have switched off animation.

video_source.label: Video from
video_source.doc: Which service the link is from. Only matters when a video is set.

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.

mark_1_ast_art.label: Artwork
mark_1_ast_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_1_ast_pos.label: Position
mark_1_ast_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_1_ast_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_1_ast_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_1_ast_show.label: Show this mark
mark_1_ast_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_1_ast_anim.label: Animation
mark_1_ast_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.

slide_sides.label: Which side the words sit on
slide_sides.doc: Alternating is the comp: words left, then right, then left, with the photo opposite. Keeping them on one side runs the text block down the same edge the whole way through and the photo always opposite it. The panel color still alternates either way — it is what stops a fixed side reading as one long slab.

slide_mobile_first.label: On a phone, what comes first
slide_mobile_first.doc: On a phone the two halves stack instead of sitting side by side, and this says which one is on top. "The words" is how it reads today. "The photo" puts the picture at the top of every slide, so the eye lands on the image first and the stack is the same every time rather than following the left-right alternation used on wide screens.

slide_split.label: How a slide moves
slide_split.doc: Together is the original: the whole slide travels sideways as one strip. As two columns keeps two boxes side by side that never move; on a change the words and the photo each slide up inside their own box, in step, so the frame holds still and only what is in it changes. On a phone the slides are one strip either way. Anyone who has switched off animation sees neither.

cta_position.label: Where the buttons sit
cta_position.doc: At the bottom is the usual place and the one the rest of the site uses. This section has no heading, so the bottom is the only position offered.

choices.foot: At the bottom of the section

btn_size.label: Size
btn_size.doc: How big this section's buttons are. "As set site-wide" follows the Buttons tab on the Site-wide page; any single button can still differ on its own row.

btn_color.label: Button color
btn_color.doc:
The color for this section's buttons. "As designed" leaves them exactly as they are. Any one button can be given its own color in the list below — this is the one they fall back to.

Light, Dark, Accent and Alt accent are ROLES — what each one looks like is set once on the Site-wide page, so changing Accent there repaints every accent button on the site. The named shades below them are fixed colors for anything that has to be one particular color.

btn_hover.label: Button hover color
btn_hover.doc:
The color this section's buttons change TO when someone points at them. "As designed" means they keep their own color and the hover effect works it out — Fill in, for instance, swaps to the opposite ink so it always shows something.

This is what was missing: only the four ROLES had a hover color, set on the Site-wide page, so a button in one of the named shades had nothing to change to and effects that work by changing color did nothing at all.

btn_style.label: Filled or outline
btn_style.doc: Filled is a solid block of color. Outline draws the color as a ring with the words in it and nothing behind. Any one button can be set differently in the list below.

btn_effect.label: Hover effect
btn_effect.doc:
What the button does when someone points at it. Lift is what every button has always done and stays the default — it rises slightly and casts a shadow. Lift and swap color does that AND flips to the opposite ink, which is the loudest of the set and best kept for one main action on a page. Underline draws a rule under the words and leaves the button still, which reads as a link — a good fit for the small buttons. Grow swells it in place. Press down pushes it into the page. Fill in floods an outline button with its color, so pair it with Outline. None holds it still.

This is the HOVER only; the way the button arrives on screen is the site-wide reveal. Anyone who has switched off animation sees no hover movement whatever is chosen.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.doc:
Buttons for this section. Add as many as you need — they sit in a row and wrap onto the next line on a narrow screen. Leave the list empty, as it is now, and the section has no buttons at all and looks exactly as it does today.

Size, color, hover color, fill and hover effect are set for the whole section above; open any button's row and the same five controls are there for that one button. Left on "Same as the section" a button follows the section, and the section follows the Site-wide page.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The words on the button. Short reads best: it is set in capitals with wide letter spacing. A button with no label is not drawn.

href.label: Link
href.doc: Where it goes. A path like /careers/ stays on this site, a full address goes off it, and mailto:someone@blacktoprg.com opens a mail window.

popup.label: Open in a pop-up
popup.doc: For a Google Form, choose Pop-up and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people to Google. A form that is set to require a Google sign-in CANNOT be shown this way — Google's sign-in page refuses to be embedded and the panel comes up blank — so that one has to stay on Open the link until its Responses settings are changed. Anything that is not a form stays on Open the link.

color.label: Color
color.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's color above. Set it to make one button stand out from the others — a main button and a quieter second one, for instance.

hover.label: Hover color
hover.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's hover color above. Set it to give one button its own hover — a main button that flips to black while the quieter ones stay put.

style.label: Filled or outline
style.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow the section. The usual pair is a filled main button next to an outline one.

effect.label: Hover effect
effect.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Hover effect, which in turn follows the site-wide one on the Site-wide page. Set it here to make one button behave differently from its neighbors.

size.label: Size
size.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow it.

modal_bg.label: Pop-up background
modal_bg.doc: The color of the panel the form opens in. Match it to the form's own Theme color in Google Forms and the two read as one surface; leave them different and you get a visible frame around the form. This cannot color the form itself — that is Google's page, on their domain.
